title: Slimline lexer + hybrid shunt for prompt-ingest: reduce prefill CPU and copies
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: High CPU and memory-copy overhead on the prefill path for short, chatty prompts causes latency spikes and increases per-token cost. Existing fastpaths handle ASCII or cached prefixes; however, switching between vectorized and fallback lexers incurs buffer copies and duplicate normalization work.

Goal: Implement a 'Slimline lexer' combined with a 'Hybrid Shunt' routing layer to 1) detect cheap fastpathable inputs without full tokenization, 2) pre-normalize in-place for cache-friendly buffers, and 3) emit an early 'kernel hint' header (sequence-length histogram + token-type flags) to the runtime so decode-side kernel selection can begin before full KV caching is materialized. Target: reduce median prefill CPU time by 40% and p95 by 30% for 0-128 token prompts, with no regression on correctness or tokenization fidelity.
acceptance_criteria: Slimline lexer integrated behind existing tokenizer feature flag
Server-side unit tests cover ASCII fastpath, UTF8 slowpath, and hybrid shunt routing
Benchmarks show >=35% median prefill CPU improvement and p95 improvement >=25% on representative chat workloads
End-to-end quality parity (<0.1% tokenization diffs on our eval corpus) for all supported models
Kernel-hint header propagated reliably to runtime and used in early-kernel selection in at least 2 kernel-selection codepaths
Rollout plan documented and telemetry dashboards created for tokenization latency, extra copies, and kernel-hint usage
implementation_notes: Design a tiny in-place normalizer that recognizes common Unicode NFC/NFKC cases and ASCII-only inputs and avoids allocating new buffers when possible

Hybrid Shunt: lightweight heuristic that classifies input into: ASCII-fast, ASCII-with-escape, UTF8-generic, cached-prefix-hit; route to vectorized lexer, ASCII escape handler, fallback UTF8 lexer, or cache return respectively
Introduce short-hash index into session-local microcache to test prefix hits without full tokenization; hash size tuned for <1% collision on top-1000 prefixes

Emit a small kernel-hint header (json-lite) containing: estimated token count, top-3 prefix candidates, ascii_ratio, and short-sequence histogram to allow runtime to choose attention kernel and KV allocation
Avoid extra memcpy by using a shared arena buffer that's pinned during prefill and can be referenced directly by the GPU upload path; add refcount guards for safety
Add feature-flag gating + config knobs (enable_shunt, shallow_hash_size, ascii_threshold) accessible via Console for gradual rollout
Tie into optimize service to suggest enabling slimline lexer for customer workloads with small prompt distribution

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Hash collisions causing incorrect cache hits -> Mitigation: conservative short-hash sizing, confirm via checksum fallback in debug builds
Risk: In-place normalization misses edge Unicode cases -> Mitigation: maintain comprehensive unicode test-suite; enable strict mode in early rollout
Risk: Kernel-hint may be ignored by runtime causing no benefit -> Mitigation: add telemetry to measure hint adoption and fallback counters; ship explicit runtime consumer flag
Risk: Shared arena buffer could increase memory residency -> Mitigation: bounded size pool per worker with LRU eviction and observable metrics
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flag gated A/B experiments on 10% of internal traffic, shadow runtime hints -> validate correctness and perf
Phase 1: enable for low-risk customers (free-tier and internal), monitor for 72h
Phase 2: ramp to 50% traffic with auto-rollback if p95 regression >5% or tokenization diff >0.2%
Phase 3: global enable and deprecation of legacy extra-copy path after 4 weeks of stable metrics
